live.instructions:
Optimize routes with Routific (https://routific.com) — answered in chat, or set up on a map in the
user's Routific account.

STEP 1 — before optimizing, ask once where they want the result, unless their request already says:
  "Do you want the plan here in chat, or set up in your Routific account so you can see it on a map and dispatch
  it to your drivers? The map needs a Routific account (free plan: 100 orders a month, sign up at
  https://plan.routific.com/signup?utm_source=mcp), and the stops are added as orders to your account."
If they mention a map, Routific, the app, drivers' phones or dispatching, that's the map. If they say "just tell
me" or similar, that's chat. Then run exactly ONE optimization for that choice — never plan in chat first and then
again on the map.

STEP 2 — chat:
- optimize_route: one driver, up to 8 stops. No sign-in, nothing saved.
- create_optimization: more stops, several drivers/vehicles, time windows, or capacity. Requires signing in;
  nothing is saved. It waits and returns the plan; only very large runs need a follow-up with get_optimization and
  get_schedule_solution.
Never split a long stop list into several optimize_route calls: separately optimized chunks aren't an optimized
route — use create_optimization instead. If they later ask for the chat plan on a map, use show_on_map and say
Routific plans it again, so the result can differ slightly.

STEP 3 — map: call show_on_map ONCE with every stop, one driver per vehicle, and the date (the day they mentioned,
otherwise today). Pass the depot as { address } in each driver's startLocation (and endLocation if they return), or
coordinates the user gave; never invent coordinates. Service time (duration) is in seconds — 300 is 5 minutes.
show_on_map adds the orders, creates the routes, optimizes only those, waits, and returns view_in_app with a short
summary. The user chose to see the plan in Routific, so the link IS the answer: start your reply with it on its own
line, bold — **🗺️ [Open in Routific →](view_in_app)** — then one or two short lines (date, stops and routes, anything
unscheduled, where the depot was placed). Don't list the stops or ETAs. From Routific they can adjust the plan and
dispatch it to their drivers' phones.

To change orders afterwards, use the ids from show_on_map, or list_routes with include_orders to find a day's
orders. Use update_orders for the same change on many orders (one call, not one per order); addTags keeps existing
tags. Tags are routing requirements (an order tagged X needs a route tagged X), so for a plain label prefer
customFields or instructions. Other tools: get_route_timeline, get_order, update_order, delete_orders.
Confirm before deleting orders. Tools that take workspaceUuid can omit it when the account has one workspace.

Talking to the user: they plan deliveries; they don't build this integration. Talk about their stops, routes,
drivers and orders in plain language. Don't mention tool names, field names, ids, HTTP codes or API details, and
don't present problems as bug reports or suggest raising them with anyone. If something didn't work, say briefly
what didn't happen and what they can do: try again, change it in Routific, or contact Routific support at
support@routific.com. Stick to helping with their routes; don't bring in unrelated company or project context.

If a tool reports that the account hit its plan's monthly order limit, tell the user to log in to their Routific
account and upgrade their plan. Don't retry or split the request.

tools.name: optimize_route
tools.title: Optimize Route
tools.description: Only for when the user chose the plan in chat. If the user hasn't said whether they want the plan here in chat or set up on a map in their Routific account, ask them first and wait for the answer — don't call any planning tool until they've chosen. Optimize the visiting order of a list of addresses (a single-vehicle delivery/service route). Returns the optimal stop sequence with an ETA and driving distance for each stop, plus total travel time and distance. Addresses are geocoded automatically; include city and region in every address for reliable results. Maximum 8 stops per request (free demo limit). Never split a longer stop list into multiple calls: chunks optimized separately are not jointly optimal, so the combined result would NOT be an optimized route. If there are more than 8 stops or several drivers, use create_optimization instead (requires signing in). Docs: https://docs.routific.com/reference/vrp-long.

stops.description: Addresses to visit, e.g. '800 Robson St, Vancouver, BC, Canada'. Always include city and region/country.

start_address.description: Where the driver starts (depot, office, home). If omitted, the first entry in `stops` is used as the starting point.

return_to_start.description: If true, the route ends back at the starting location. Default false.

departure_time.description: Departure time in 24h hh:mm format used to compute ETAs. Default "09:00".

tools.name: create_optimization
tools.title: Create Optimization (Routific account)
tools.description: Only for when the user chose the plan in chat. If the user hasn't said whether they want the plan here in chat or set up on a map in their Routific account, ask them first and wait for the answer — don't call any planning tool until they've chosen. Run a full multi-vehicle route optimization on YOUR Routific organization (requires signing in). This is a self-contained 'one-off' schedule: pass the fleet inline as `routesData` (vehicles, up to 500) and the stops inline as `ordersData` (deliveries/visits, up to 5,000) — no workspace or pre-created records are needed. The engine assigns every order to a route while respecting time windows, capacity, and tags. Waits for the result (up to ~45s) and returns the solved plan: each vehicle's stops in order with ETAs, plus anything left unscheduled. Very large runs may still be going when it returns; then it gives an actionUuid to check with get_optimization and fetch with get_schedule_solution. Nothing is saved to the user's workspace. Docs: https://api-docs.routific.com/reference/one-off-scheduling.

name.description: Human-readable vehicle or driver name (must be unique).

constraints.description: Shift window, capacity, start/end locations, and tags for this vehicle.

startTime.description: Earliest the vehicle can start its shift, 24h HH:mm.

endTime.description: Latest the vehicle must finish its shift, 24h HH:mm.

capacity.description: Total load the vehicle can carry; compared against each order's `load`.

startLocations.description: Where the vehicle starts its shift (the depot).

address.description: Street address, including city and region/country (e.g. '800 Robson St, Vancouver, BC, Canada'). Provide this and/or latitude+longitude.

endLocations.description: Where the vehicle ends its shift. Omit to end at the final stop.

address.description: Street address, including city and region/country (e.g. '800 Robson St, Vancouver, BC, Canada'). Provide this and/or latitude+longitude.

tags.description: Skills/zones this vehicle can serve; matched against each order's `tags`.

routesData.description: The fleet: the vehicles/drivers orders can be scheduled onto (max 500).

address.description: Street address, including city and region/country (e.g. '800 Robson St, Vancouver, BC, Canada'). Provide this and/or latitude+longitude.

duration.description: Service time spent at the stop, in seconds (e.g. 900 for 15 minutes).

load.description: Capacity units this order consumes; compared against a route's `capacity`.

timeWindows.description: Allowed arrival windows for this stop. Omit to allow any time.

tags.description: Requirements for this stop; matched against a route's `tags`.

ordersData.description: The stops to schedule: deliveries or visits (max 5,000).

minimizeRoutes.description: Solve with the fewest vehicles possible.

balanceType.description: Balance workload across vehicles: 'time' evens out working time, 'orders' evens out stop counts, 'none' disables.

flexibleStartTime.description: Allow vehicles to start later than their `startTime` to reduce idle waiting.

squashDuration.description: Reduce service duration, in seconds, for consecutive stops at the same location.

defaultOrderDuration.description: Service time, in seconds, for orders that omit their own `duration` (e.g. 900 for 15 minutes).

allowCapacityOverload.description: Permit routes to exceed vehicle capacity.

allowRouteOvertime.description: Permit routes to run past the vehicle's `endTime`.

allowVisitLateness.description: Permit arrival after an order's time window.

tools.name: get_optimization
tools.title: Get Optimization Result
tools.description: Poll the status/result of an optimization started with `create_optimization`, by its actionUuid. Returns `{ status }` while the job is `pending`, and the solved schedule once the status is `finished` (or an error once `failed`). Docs: https://api-docs.routific.com/reference/fetch-schedule-status.

tools.name: show_on_map
tools.title: Show on a Map in Routific
tools.description: Only for when the user chose the map in Routific (or asked for Routific, a map, or dispatch). If the user hasn't said whether they want the plan here in chat or set up on a map in their Routific account, ask them first and wait for the answer — don't call any planning tool until they've chosen. Put a plan on the map in the user's Routific account in ONE call: adds the stops as orders for the date, creates a route per driver (depot addresses are looked up on the map), optimizes only those orders onto those routes, waits for the result, and returns the 'Open in Routific' link (view_in_app) with a short summary — no stop list, since the user sees the plan in Routific. Use this when the user wants the result on a map / in Routific — instead of, not after, optimizing in chat. Nothing else in their workspace is touched. Orders count toward their plan. Answer as the result's `reply` field says: link first.

workspaceUuid.description: Workspace uuid from list_workspaces. Optional when the account has exactly one workspace.

address.description: Full street address with city and region, e.g. '800 Robson St, Vancouver, BC, Canada'.

latitude.description: Only if the user gave exact coordinates; the address is still shown.

name.description: Customer or stop name. Defaults to the address.

packages.description: Package barcodes for the driver to scan.

customFields.description: Values for custom fields that already exist on the account (they aren't created here).

stops.description: Every stop, once each (not the depot).

startLocation.description: { address } (looked up on the map) or { latitude, longitude }. Never invent coordinates.

endLocation.description: Usually the same as startLocation when they return to the depot.

minimizeRoutes.description: Solve with the fewest vehicles possible.

balanceType.description: Balance workload across vehicles: 'time' evens out working time, 'orders' evens out stop counts, 'none' disables.

flexibleStartTime.description: Allow vehicles to start later than their `startTime` to reduce idle waiting.

squashDuration.description: Reduce service duration, in seconds, for consecutive stops at the same location.

defaultOrderDuration.description: Service time, in seconds, for orders that omit their own `duration` (e.g. 900 for 15 minutes).

allowCapacityOverload.description: Permit routes to exceed vehicle capacity.

allowRouteOvertime.description: Permit routes to run past the vehicle's `endTime`.

allowVisitLateness.description: Permit arrival after an order's time window.

tools.name: schedule_orders
tools.title: Schedule Orders (in workspace)
tools.description: Run Routific's optimizer on the user's workspace for a date: assigns the orders to the routes and sequences each route, like the Schedule button in the app. With only a date, it schedules every unscheduled order for that date across all unlocked routes; pass orders/routes to restrict it. The result is saved in the workspace. When setting up a plan from chat, pass only the orders and routes you just created. Waits for the run to finish (up to ~45s) and returns how many orders were scheduled; then share view_in_app as an 'Open in Routific' link. If it's still running when it returns, check again with `get_schedule_action`. Docs: https://api-docs.routific.com/reference/schedule-orders.

workspaceUuid.description: Workspace uuid from list_workspaces. Optional when the account has exactly one workspace.

minimizeRoutes.description: Solve with the fewest vehicles possible.

balanceType.description: Balance workload across vehicles: 'time' evens out working time, 'orders' evens out stop counts, 'none' disables.

flexibleStartTime.description: Allow vehicles to start later than their `startTime` to reduce idle waiting.

squashDuration.description: Reduce service duration, in seconds, for consecutive stops at the same location.

defaultOrderDuration.description: Service time, in seconds, for orders that omit their own `duration` (e.g. 900 for 15 minutes).

allowCapacityOverload.description: Permit routes to exceed vehicle capacity.

allowRouteOvertime.description: Permit routes to run past the vehicle's `endTime`.

allowVisitLateness.description: Permit arrival after an order's time window.

tools.name: list_schedules
tools.title: List Schedules
tools.description: List schedules (keyset-paginated). Filter by workspace, date, or status.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's `nextCursor`.

tools.name: get_schedule_action
tools.title: Get Schedule Action Status
tools.description: Poll a schedule action's status by its actionUuid.

tools.name: get_schedule_solution
tools.title: Get Schedule Solution
tools.description: Fetch the full solved solution of a finished optimization, by its actionUuid: `{ routes, orders, unscheduledOrders }` — the per-vehicle stop sequences with ETAs, plus any orders that could not be scheduled. Call this once `get_optimization` reports the action `finished` (use the same actionUuid returned by `create_optimization`). Docs: https://api-docs.routific.com/reference/fetch-scheduled-solution.

actionUuid.description: The actionUuid returned by create_optimization (status must be `finished`).

tools.name: list_routes
tools.title: List Routes
tools.description: List a workspace's routes for a date: uuid, name, driver, status, order count, working time, distance. Set include_orders to also get each route's order uuids in stop order — the way to find a day's orders for follow-up edits (update_order / update_orders / delete_orders). Docs: https://api-docs.routific.com/reference/fetch-routes.

workspaceUuid.description: Workspace uuid from list_workspaces. Optional when the account has exactly one workspace.

include_orders.description: Also return each route's order uuids (one extra read per route).

tools.name: get_route
tools.title: Get Route
tools.description: Get a single route by its uuid.

tools.name: get_route_timeline
tools.title: Get Route Timeline
tools.description: Get a route's timeline (stops in order with ETAs), keyset-paginated.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's `nextCursor`.

tools.name: create_routes
tools.title: Create Routes
tools.description: Create routes in a workspace (batch, max 50). Each route: { name, date (ISO8601), startTime, endTime (military time), startLocation?, endLocation?, capacity?, tags? }. One route per driver or vehicle. startLocation/endLocation: pass { address } (full street address with city and region — it's looked up on the map for you) or { latitude, longitude }. Never invent coordinates. The result lists where each address was placed under `geocoded_depots`; tell the user, so a wrong match is caught. Omit the locations if the user hasn't given a depot.

workspaceUuid.description: Workspace uuid from list_workspaces. Optional when the account has exactly one workspace.

tools.name: get_order
tools.title: Get Order
tools.description: Get a single order (visit) by its uuid.

tools.name: create_orders
tools.title: Create Orders
tools.description: Create orders (visits) in a workspace (batch). Each order: { locations (required): [{ address, latitude?, longitude? }], name?, email?, duration? (service time in SECONDS, e.g. 300 for 5 minutes), phone?, instructions?, load?, timeWindows?, packages?, tags?, customFields?, deliveryDate? }. Set deliveryDate (YYYY-MM-DD) so the orders can be scheduled for that day with schedule_orders. Orders count toward the account's monthly plan.

workspaceUuid.description: Workspace uuid from list_workspaces. Optional when the account has exactly one workspace.

tools.name: update_order
tools.title: Update Order
tools.description: Change fields on an existing order (scheduled or not). Pass ONLY the fields to change — everything else is kept; null clears a field. Pass `locations` to change the address (it re-geocodes); `duration` is service time in SECONDS (300 = 5 minutes). Editing a scheduled order re-times its route and may be async (returns an action to poll with `get_order_action`).

order.description: Only the fields to change, e.g. { timeWindows: [{ startTime: '09:00', endTime: '12:00' }] }.

tools.name: update_orders
tools.title: Update Orders (bulk)
tools.description: Apply the same change to many orders in one call (up to 200) — use this instead of calling update_order once per order. Pass the order uuids (from show_on_map or list_routes with include_orders), the fields to change in `order` (everything else is kept; duration is in SECONDS), and/or addTags / removeTags to change tags while keeping the existing ones. Note: tags are routing requirements — an order tagged X can only go on a route tagged X — so for a plain label prefer customFields or instructions. Returns per-order results.

order.description: Fields to set on every order, e.g. { instructions: 'Leave at door' }.

addTags.description: Tags to add, keeping each order's existing tags.

tools.name: delete_order
tools.title: Delete Order
tools.description: Permanently delete a single order by uuid, including one already on a route (the route is re-timed). Deleting a scheduled order is async (poll with `get_order_action`). Only call this after the user has explicitly confirmed — it can't be undone.

tools.name: delete_orders
tools.title: Delete Orders (bulk)
tools.description: Permanently delete multiple orders in a workspace by uuid (max 500), including ones already on a route. May be async (poll with `get_order_action`). Only call this after the user has explicitly confirmed — it can't be undone.

workspaceUuid.description: Workspace uuid from list_workspaces. Optional when the account has exactly one workspace.

tools.name: get_order_action
tools.title: Get Order Action Status
tools.description: Poll an order async action (update/delete) by its actionUuid.

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.title: List Workspaces
tools.description: List the organization's workspaces (keyset-paginated). Workspaces scope routes/orders.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's `nextCursor`.

tools.name: get_order
tools.title: Get Order
tools.description: Get a single order (visit) by its uuid.

tools.name: create_orders
tools.title: Create Orders
tools.description: Create orders (visits) in a workspace (batch). Each order: { locations (required): [{ address, latitude?, longitude? }], name?, email?, duration? (service time in SECONDS, e.g. 300 for 5 minutes), phone?, instructions?, load?, timeWindows?, packages?, tags?, customFields?, deliveryDate? }. Set deliveryDate (YYYY-MM-DD) so the orders can be scheduled for that day with schedule_orders. Orders count toward the account's monthly plan.

workspaceUuid.description: Workspace uuid from list_workspaces. Optional when the account has exactly one workspace.

tools.name: update_order
tools.title: Update Order
tools.description: Change fields on an existing order (scheduled or not). Pass ONLY the fields to change — everything else is kept; null clears a field. Pass `locations` to change the address (it re-geocodes); `duration` is service time in SECONDS (300 = 5 minutes). Editing a scheduled order re-times its route and may be async (returns an action to poll with `get_order_action`).

order.description: Only the fields to change, e.g. { timeWindows: [{ startTime: '09:00', endTime: '12:00' }] }.

tools.name: update_orders
tools.title: Update Orders (bulk)
tools.description: Apply the same change to many orders in one call (up to 200) — use this instead of calling update_order once per order. Pass the order uuids (from show_on_map or list_routes with include_orders), the fields to change in `order` (everything else is kept; duration is in SECONDS), and/or addTags / removeTags to change tags while keeping the existing ones. Note: tags are routing requirements — an order tagged X can only go on a route tagged X — so for a plain label prefer customFields or instructions. Returns per-order results.

order.description: Fields to set on every order, e.g. { instructions: 'Leave at door' }.

addTags.description: Tags to add, keeping each order's existing tags.

tools.name: delete_order
tools.title: Delete Order
tools.description: Permanently delete a single order by uuid, including one already on a route (the route is re-timed). Deleting a scheduled order is async (poll with `get_order_action`). Only call this after the user has explicitly confirmed — it can't be undone.

tools.name: delete_orders
tools.title: Delete Orders (bulk)
tools.description: Permanently delete multiple orders in a workspace by uuid (max 500), including ones already on a route. May be async (poll with `get_order_action`). Only call this after the user has explicitly confirmed — it can't be undone.

workspaceUuid.description: Workspace uuid from list_workspaces. Optional when the account has exactly one workspace.

tools.name: get_order_action
tools.title: Get Order Action Status
tools.description: Poll an order async action (update/delete) by its actionUuid.

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.title: List Workspaces
tools.description: List the organization's workspaces (keyset-paginated). Workspaces scope routes/orders.
